newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks gripped by seasonal lethargy.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks gripped by seasonal lethargy.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks continued to edge down on the lack of any market-specific good news and as December's holiday mood took a grip on sentiment, brokers said.
The all share index closed 3.4 points down at 601.8. Hayleys fell five rupees to 175, National Development Bank four to 201.
"The closer the index comes to 590 to 600 points, there is more likelihood of some buying returning," said Channa Kurukulasuriya, head of research at Lanka Securities.
In the absence of any market moving news, and the upcoming December holiday season, the index would remain at current levels, he said.
"The index should move between about 590 and 610 points until January if there is no market-specific news," said Dimuthu Abeysekera a broker at Allied Phillips Securities.
Turnover was 18.2 million rupees on 1.7 million shares.
Main volumes were foreign buying of 116,800 Dockyard at 14.5 rupees and 74,000 Sampath Bank at 46, and local buying of one million Kelani Tyre at 6.25.
The market was unmoved by Tuesday's launch of Century Growth Fund, Sri Lanka's first equity fund. --Prithi Kodagoda (941) - 434319
